steps.name: Load, QC-align, filter and normalize counts
steps.question: Given the 12000 x 121 Salmon gene-level count matrix and the 120-sample metadata (case vs control), how should samples be aligned, low-count genes filtered, and counts normalized to produce an expression matrix suitable for co-expression network construction?
acceptance_criteria: Counts matrix (12000 genes x up to 121 samples) is read and intersected with the 120-sample metadata by sample ID; any sample present in counts but absent from metadata is dropped and the drop is reported explicitly
Genes with near-zero variance or very low counts across samples are filtered (e.g. minimum count/expression threshold) with the number of genes retained reported
A variance-stabilizing transform (DESeq2 vst or vst-equivalent) is applied to raw counts to produce an approximately homoskedastic expression matrix appropriate for WGCNA
Output includes the final aligned expression matrix (genes x 120 samples) and the aligned case/control metadata, saved for downstream steps
Sample and gene filtering decisions and resulting dimensions are reported

steps.name: WGCNA network construction and module detection
steps.question: Across all 120 whole-blood samples (case and control combined), what co-expression modules do the ~12000 genes form, using the normalized expression matrix from T1S1?
acceptance_criteria: Sample network check for outliers is performed (e.g. hierarchical clustering / sample connectivity) prior to network construction, and any excluded outlier samples are reported by ID
Soft-thresholding power is chosen by scale-free topology fit criterion (targeting R^2 >= 0.8 where achievable) and the choice is justified with the fit curve values

A signed or signed-hybrid co-expression network and topological overlap matrix are constructed and modules are detected via dynamic tree cut on the resulting dendrogram, with a stated minimum module size
Module eigengenes are computed for every detected module, and modules with highly correlated eigengenes are merged (with the merge height threshold stated)
Output includes: gene-to-module assignment table, module eigengene matrix (samples x modules), count of modules detected, and count of genes in the unassigned/grey module
Module detection is performed WITHOUT using the case/control label as input, so downstream trait association is not circular

steps.name: Module-trait association with case vs control status
steps.question: Which of the co-expression modules detected in T1S2 have module eigengenes that significantly differ between the 60 cases and 60 controls?
acceptance_criteria: Each module eigengene from T1S2 is tested for association with the binary case/control status (e.g. eigengene-trait correlation with Student asymptotic p-value, or Welch t-test/Wilcoxon comparing eigengene values between the two groups)
P-values are corrected for multiple testing across all modules (e.g. Benjamini-Hochberg FDR) and both raw and adjusted p-values are reported per module
A ranked table of modules by trait association strength and significance is produced, naming modules by their WGCNA color/ID and reporting module size (gene count)
For each significant module (FDR < 0.05), the direction of association (higher/lower eigengene in cases vs controls) is stated explicitly
If no module reaches significance after correction, this null result is reported plainly rather than highlighting nominal (uncorrected) hits as findings

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of case/control-associated modules
steps.question: What biological pathways are over-represented among the genes in the co-expression modules found in T1S3 to significantly track case vs control status?
acceptance_criteria: Over-representation analysis is run separately for each significant (FDR < 0.05) module's gene set from T1S3, using the ~12000-gene filtered set from T1S1 as the statistical background rather than the whole genome
Human WikiPathways gene sets (HGNC symbols) are used as the pathway reference; if unavailable at run time, the step reports the gap rather than substituting a non-human resource
Output includes, per module, top enriched pathways with adjusted p-values (e.g. BH-FDR) and the overlapping gene lists
If T1S3 found no significant modules, this step reports that no enrichment was run rather than enriching an arbitrary or nominal module set

plan.title: WGCNA co-expression modules vs case/control status
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is bulk RNA-seq whole-blood gene-level counts from Salmon (12000 genes x 121 samples with metadata for 120: 60 case / 60 control, unpaired, single batch). The research question asks for co-expression modules across all 120 samples and which modules associate with case vs control. This is a classic WGCNA workflow: (1) load and QC-align counts to metadata, filter low-expressed genes, apply a variance-stabilizing normalization suited to raw counts (DESeq2 vst or similar) since WGCNA requires approximately homoskedastic, normalized expression rather than raw counts; (2) run WGCNA network construction and module detection (soft-thresholding power selection, topological overlap matrix, dynamic tree cut) to define modules across the full 120-sample cohort, independent of case/control label, to avoid circularity; (3) correlate module eigengenes with the binary case/control trait to find which modules track disease status, with multiple-testing correction across modules; (4) functionally characterize the case/control-associated modules using WikiPathways human pathway gene sets (present in the environment) via over-representation analysis, to give biological interpretation to genes within tracking modules. Steps are ordered so that module discovery (unsupervised) precedes and is separate from the trait-association test, preserving the appropriate independence between clustering and the case/control comparison.
